name: Stereolab
label: Drag City
lede: Stereolab took its name from a hi-fi demonstration record and spent two decades setting Lætitia Sadier's French vocals and Marxist-flavored lyrics against Farfisa drones. By one count they sold 300,000 albums in America without once pretending to be a rock band.

eras.title: McCarthy ends, softly
eras.text: Tim Gane spent the late 1980s in McCarthy, a left-wing indie-pop band from Barking, and met Lætitia Sadier after a McCarthy show in Paris. When McCarthy ended in 1990, the two had the start of a new band.

years.h: Tim Gane co-founds McCarthy in Barking, east London
years.p: Jangly indie pop with left-wing lyrics, Gane on guitar, and the band he keeps through the rest of the decade.

years.h: Lætitia Sadier meets Tim Gane at a McCarthy gig in Paris
years.p: Sadier, a Parisian, and Gane become a couple that lasts 14 years.

years.h: McCarthy's last album has Sadier on it
years.p: Banking, Violence and the Inner Life Today is the final McCarthy record. The band folds soon after, softly by Gane's account.
years.xp:
"It ended very softly," Gane told Chickfactor. By his telling McCarthy was mostly funny and mostly fun, with no big blow-up at the end.

Out of it came Stereolab: Gane and Sadier with Martin Kean on bass (ex-[[The Chills|90b5813d-fbd7-4539-89d5-034094f64a2e]]), Joe Dilworth on drums (from [[Th' Faith Healers|d9c7e489-54c0-413b-b7a5-4af14a2fd305]]) and Gina Morris on backing vocals.

years.h: A hi-fi demo record from Vanguard gives the band its name
years.p: Vanguard Records ran a Stereolab series built to show off stereo effects. Gane and Sadier borrow the name for the new band.

eras.title: Their own label, then Elektra's money
eras.text: Stereolab started Duophonic before it had a record to put on it, and built a following on limited singles and EPs. Mary Hansen and Andy Ramsay arrived, and by 1993 Elektra was paying for the American releases while Duophonic kept the UK.

years.h: Duophonic's first release is Super 45, and it's Stereolab's too
years.p: A May 1991 EP on the band's own label, put out before anyone outside their circle had heard them.
years.xp: Gane, Sadier and their manager Martin Pike set the label up as Duophonic Super 45s. Gane said the plan was to put out 7- and 10-inch records, "to just do one a month."

years.cap: Mary Hansen and Lætitia Sadier, Central Park, New York, July 22, 1995
years.h: Mary Hansen, an Australian in London, joins as second voice
years.p: Hansen, who has known Gane since McCarthy days, takes second voice and guitar. Andy Ramsay takes over the drums and Duncan Brown the bass.
years.xp:
Hansen was born in Maryborough, Queensland, in 1966, the daughter of a Labor politician and a light opera singer. She moved to London in 1988 and sang backing vocals with the Wolfhounds before Stereolab.

She played on six Stereolab albums, from 1993 to 2001, and sang lead on the odd song.

years.h: Peng!, the first Stereolab album, comes out on Too Pure
years.p: Motorik drone under Sadier's cool French-accented singing, on the London label Too Pure.

q: We're too polite to demand anything, although we always ask for cider.
years.h: Switched On collects the singles that sold out
years.p: Too Pure in the UK and Slumberland Records in the US put out the early singles together. Gane on the band's backstage demands.
years.xp:
The band told Chickfactor they chased the Slumberland single because not much was happening for them in America and it might get them noticed. The colored sleeve they wanted never got made.

In the same interview Gane judged their chances plainly: "Stereolab couldn't get arrested if they tried."

yt: Live at the Kennel Club, San Francisco, Oct 27, 1993
years.h: Katharine Gifford takes the keyboards, Sean O'Hagan the guitar
years.p: [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]] leader O'Hagan joins for a spell on guitar and keys.

years.h: A lounge-exotica mini-album gets Elektra interested
years.p: The Groop Played "Space Age Bachelor Pad Music" comes out on Too Pure on March 22 and lifts Stereolab's profile enough to land an American deal with Elektra Records.
years.xp: The record leans on 1950s and 60s easy listening, the Juan Esquivel and Martin Denny end of the shelf. Encyclopedia.com says the Farfisa organs the band picked up in thrift shops gave Gane the "bit of spillage" he wanted in the sound.

years.cap: Duophonic in the UK, Elektra in the US
years.h: Elektra takes America, Duophonic keeps the UK for Transient Random-Noise Bursts
years.p: The second album comes out in August 1993 on both labels at once, a split the band holds for the next decade.
years.xp: The deal was unusual for a major: Stereolab kept their own label at home and handed Elektra the US. Duophonic stayed the band's base for everything they released after.

eras.title: Marx on the charts, Lollapalooza on the small stage
eras.text: A charting single and a pop song about boom and bust put Stereolab in the music press and on American summer bills. The line-up kept shifting. Gane and Sadier didn't.

years.h: Stereolab can't press enough Jenny Ondioline EPs to meet demand
years.p: The EP enters the UK Singles Chart at number 75, the band's first chart entry.

years.h: Mars Audiac Quintet has a pop single about boom and bust
years.p: The third album, out in August 1994, carries "Ping Pong", a bright tune that explains capitalism's boom-and-bust cycles. The press hears Marx.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the lyric "a plainspoken explanation of one of the central tenets of Marxian economic analysis."

q: None of us are Marxists. I've never even read Marx.
years.h: The press makes Stereolab the Marxist band
years.p: Gane's reply: none of them were. The lyrics, mostly Sadier's, came from Guy Debord and the Situationists, not party tracts.
years.xp:
Debord's The Society of the Spectacle and the Situationists and Surrealists shaped the words more than party politics did. Sadier's side project, Monade, is named for an idea from the philosopher Cornelius Castoriadis.

Sadier told Chickfactor: "Create a disturbance is the best way we thought of to make people think."

years.h: Sean O'Hagan trades full membership for guest spots
years.p: After Mars Audiac Quintet he steps back to concentrate on [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]], and keeps turning up on Stereolab records.

years.h: Refried Ectoplasm sends more singles to America through Drag City
years.p: Switched On volume two has 13 tracks, including "French Disko". Duophonic issues it in the UK and Drag City in the US, the start of Stereolab's run with the Chicago label.
years.xp: Drag City lists it as DC82, a double LP or CD, and sells it as "a companion piece to the second copy of this record that you'll buy when you wear the first one out."

years.h: Stereolab ride the Lollapalooza second stage
years.p: Sonic Youth and Pavement have the main bill on the 1995 tour; Stereolab take the small stage and a new American audience.
years.xp: Encyclopedia.com credits the 1995 second stage with putting Stereolab in front of a wide alternative audience, a year before Emperor Tomato Ketchup.

years.h: Morgane Lhote is told to learn 30 songs before she's in
years.p: Katharine Gifford and Duncan Brown leave. Richard Harrison takes the bass.

eras.title: Chicago, loops and horns
eras.text: With John McEntire of Tortoise in Chicago, Stereolab swapped drone for loops, vibraphone and horns. By August 1999, Wikipedia's sources say, they had sold 300,000 albums in America.

years.h: Emperor Tomato Ketchup swaps drone for loops
years.p: Recorded at Blackwing in London and Idful in Chicago with [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], and named for a 1971 Shūji Terayama film.
years.xp:
Gane said the loop-based sound came out of being stuck. Working on a cover of [[The Godz|d01198aa-b733-4816-9393-cd0cb915db37]]' "ABC", he looped four of its notes, and they became an early take on "Percolator".

Duophonic released it in the UK on March 18, 1996 (number 27 on the chart) and Elektra in the US on April 9. By August 1997 it had sold more than 46,000 copies in America. Pitchfork gave it a 9.4.

years.h: Dots and Loops is the first Stereolab album on the Billboard 200
years.p: It peaks at number 111, with [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and Jan St. Werner of [[Mouse on Mars|4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce]] on board.

years.h: A seven-month tour ends, and Gane and Sadier's child arrives
years.p: Stereolab pauses live work for a while.

years.h: A third Switched On arrives as a 25-track roundup
years.p: Aluminum Tunes draws on singles and rarities from the Mars Audiac Quintet era onward, including the whole Amorphous Body Study Center EP. Duophonic and Drag City issue it.

years.cap: Stereolab at the Belly Up, Solana Beach, California, November 19, 1999
yt: Live at the Variety Playhouse, Atlanta, 1999
years.h: Cobra and Phases gets two producers and middling reviews
years.p: [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] co-produce the sixth album, which peaks at 154 in America. Simon Johns is now on bass.
years.xp: By August 1999, Wikipedia's sources put Stereolab's US album sales at 300,000 copies.

eras.title: Losing Mary Hansen
eras.text: In 2002 Gane and Sadier ended their relationship, the band began building a studio in France, and on December 9 Hansen was killed while cycling in London. Stereolab kept going, and dedicated the next album to her.

years.h: Sound-Dust wins back the critics
years.p: [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] and [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] produce again, and reviewers like it better than Cobra and Phases.

years.h: Stereolab starts building a studio north of Bordeaux
years.p: The French countryside gets a recording room. The same year, Gane and Sadier end their 14-year relationship.

years.h: Mary Hansen is killed by a lorry while cycling in London
years.p: Hansen, Stereolab's second voice and guitarist since 1992, was 36.
years.xp:
The band's statement read: "The suddenness of her death has shocked the band." She died on December 9, 2002.

Hansen also sang with [[The High Llamas|df3131d7-9cbc-4ad5-945a-09e979f003f4]], [[Mouse on Mars|4d4f5d92-0589-42fa-bc0e-1bd73e17a2ce]], Moonshake and Brokeback, and fronted her own band, Schema. A 2004 EP, Hybird, gathered three of her earlier limited-run tracks and her artwork, with a last track finished by Ramsay.

years.h: Instant 0 in the Universe is the first record without Hansen
years.p: An EP made at the band's new studio in France.

years.cap: Stereolab at Hebbel am Ufer, Berlin, May 15, 2006
years.h: Margerine Eclipse closes the Elektra years with a song for Hansen
years.p: "Feel and Triple" is Sadier's tribute to Mary Hansen. Elektra folds the same year.
years.xp: The eighth album is dedicated to Hansen and was the band's last for Elektra.

eras.title: One record for 4AD, then a hiatus
eras.text: Without a major label, Stereolab put out limited singles (collected as Fab Four Suture in 2006) and one brisk pop record for 4AD. In 2009 their manager announced a pause that lasted a decade.

years.h: Stereolab sign with 4AD for Chemical Chords
years.p: Short, horn-lit pop songs, issued by Duophonic with 4AD, on the label's roster for this one album.

years.cap: Stereolab at the Glass House, September 21, 2008
years.h: Manager Martin Pike announces an indefinite break
years.p: Stereolab pauses so the members can work on other projects.

years.h: Not Music clears out the Chemical Chords leftovers
years.p: Songs recorded during the Chemical Chords sessions come out as Stereolab's last album for 15 years.

eras.title: The reissues bring them back
eras.text: Expanded reissues on Warp Records brought Stereolab back on stage in 2019 after ten years away. A new album followed in 2025.

years.cap: Tim Gane and Andy Ramsay, San Fran, Wellington, March 3, 2020
years.h: Stereolab announce a tour and start reissuing the albums on Warp
years.p: It's the group's first live run since 2009, across Europe and the US. Expanded, remastered albums start arriving through Duophonic and Warp.

years.h: Stereolab play their first show in ten years at Primavera Sound
years.p: Gane, Sadier and Ramsay take the stage in Barcelona, then play Primavera Porto the following weekend.

years.h: Fans get "unsolicited Stereolab material" in the mail
years.p: The packages hold a new song and arrive exactly 16 years after the hiatus announcement.
years.xp: Newsletter subscribers got a word-search puzzle and posters went up in cities around the world. The official announcement came on April 8.

years.h: The first new album in 15 years, Instant Holograms on Metal Film, reaches number 29 in the UK
years.p: Gane and Sadier with Ramsay, Joe Watson and Xavi Muñoz, plus [[Bitchin Bajas|6243b9cb-63ad-438d-88f9-50c35d3f1088]]' Cooper Crain and Rob Frye, recorded at Press Play studio in London.
years.xp:
Duophonic UHF Disks and Warp released it on May 23, 2025. Metacritic scores it 84 out of 100; Pitchfork gave it a 7.8.

The lead single, "Aerial Troubles", came out on April 8 with a retro video directed by Laurent Askienazy.
